original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume m <= p < hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that an m-element subset A satisfies |h_hat A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
target_in_paper: The nearest official formulation is Section 0.3, Conjecture 0.3.5, in the section "Minimum size of h-fold restricted sumsets." It is posed as the inverse-problem analogue, for restricted sumsets, of the ordinary-sumset statements Theorem 0.2.2 and Conjecture 0.2.3. Your draft is targeting this conjecture rather than the ordinary sumset case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient setting (a finite abelian group G of order n), the correct prime parameter p as the smallest prime divisor of n, the exact parameter range m ≤ p < hm - h^2 + 1, the target extremal value p, and the correct structural conclusion that A should be contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p. Those are exactly the core ingredients of Conjecture 0.3.5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
missing_details: The notation \hat{h}A should be defined explicitly as the h-fold restricted sumset: \hat{h}A := {a_1+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\ldots,a_h \in A are pairwise distinct}. The paper fixes this notation in the opening notation section. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
It should be stated explicitly that G is written additively and that A is an m-subset of G, i.e. |A| = m. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
The quantifiers on h and m should be made explicit: they are positive integers, and in the restricted-sumset setting the paper assumes h ≤ m. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))

To be fully paper-faithful, it helps to signal that this is an inverse problem from the restricted-sumset section, asked in the parameter range where the companion direct conjecture predicts that the minimum possible value is p. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
refined_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, let h and m be positive integers with m ≤ p < hm - h^2 + 1, and for each m-subset A ⊆ G define the h-fold restricted sumset by \hat{h}A := {a_1+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\ldots,a_h \in A are pairwise distinct}. Is it true that, for every m-subset A of G, one has |\hat{h}A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset x+H of some subgroup H ≤ G with |H| = p? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
justification: This rewrite stays as close as possible to the paper because Conjecture 0.3.5 is stated in essentially exactly this form in the restricted-sumset section, immediately after the companion direct conjecture and as the restricted-sumset analogue of the ordinary-sumset inverse problems Theorem 0.2.2 and Conjecture 0.2.3. The only real repairs needed were to define the operator \hat{h}A and to make the ambient conventions explicit so that the question is fully stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
